publications.title: Replication Package - Cognitive Equity in Educational Brain-Computer Interfaces: Structured Review Materials
authors: Anonymous (author names withheld for peer review)
publications.abstract: Replication package for a structured review of ethical, legal and governance discourse on brain-computer interface (BCI) and neurotechnology deployment in educational settings, charted against a five-domain conditional structure of cognitive equity (access, measurement, autonomy, enhancement, neuro-data governance). Contents: full review protocol (eligibility, sources, selection, charting, appraisal, synthesis, update and saturation rule); frozen verbatim search strings for all executed sources (PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, ERIC, Embase, OpenAlex including the Chinese-language block, PhilPapers, plus supplementary Crossref, arXiv and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses searches); per-source execution log with registered counts and platform-access notes; charting codebook with an argument-quality scale; screening-governance, reliability and audit documentation; and self-contained analysis scripts (Monte-Carlo chi-square tests on the corpus composition tables). Frozen count chain: 20,338 identified - 17,489 unique after deduplication - 684 included by dual-pass screening with calibrated arbitration - 79 added by citation chasing over 18,765 cited works - 759 after title-level deduplication - 48 removed by charting-stage audit - 711 records analysed. The composition tests are computed on the 709 analysed records with complete publication-year metadata. Author identities are withheld during peer review. Record-level datasets are deposited separately upon acceptance. v1.1 corrects the column-order labels in the corpus-composition test script (chi-square statistics unchanged) and documents the 709/711 subset relation. Prior protocol registration: DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/NAVJ8.
publications.source_detail: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

publications.title: Fixed-Surface Multidimensional Tokenization (FSMT-001): Master Research Project and Execution Prompt
publications.abstract: A consolidated research-programme draft for Fixed-Surface Multidimensional Tokenization (FSMT-001): a fixed manuscript as an immutable substrate, with a separate computational layer assigning states to its negative-space coordinates through a formal legend and tokenizer, and an independent decoder to reconstruct the encoded information without modifying the original. The draft (v0.1) consolidates the FSMT-001 v0.1.0 master document into a programme of seven architecture layers, ten research questions, nine proposed experiments, six comparison baselines, twelve evaluation criteria and ten deliverables, with the LUMa Master Language Research Charter v0.1.0 included as a related source. Status: PROPOSED. No independent human expert review has been conducted. The originator provides high-level conceptual direction and retains final authority over publication approval, but does not claim to have performed a detailed technical validation. No mathematical model, prototype, corpus, or experimental results exist; no novelty claim is made — prior-art investigation is mandatory before any novelty claim. AI-assistance disclosure: research architecture by Athena (ChatGPT), archiving by Baby Lucy (Meta AI), consolidated draft assembled and revised by Lucy (Muse AI).

publications.title: IMPROVING EFL STUDENTS' WRITING SKILLS THROUGH DIGITAL LEARNING PLATFORMS
publications.abstract: Writing is a complex skill for EFL (English as a Foreign Language) learners because it involves grammatical competence, vocabulary knowledge, idea organization, and the ability to convey meaning coherently. Technological developments have introduced various digital platforms that can support writing instruction, particularly through collaborative features, feedback, and assessment tools. This article aims to examine the roles and uses of digital learning platforms in EFL writing instruction based on previous research. This study employed a literature review method involving 15 scholarly publications published between 2021 and 2025. The data were analyzed thematically by categorizing the findings according to the functions of technology in writing instruction. The review identified three major themes. First, Google Docs supports collaborative writing through shared text production and editing, interaction among learners, and engagement in the writing process. Second, artificial intelligence-based technologies, particularly ChatGPT, provide alternative sources of feedback and support for writing revision, although the accuracy and relevance of their outputs still require evaluation and teacher guidance. Third, AI-based tools can serve as additional resources for writing assessment; however, differences between human and AI scoring indicate that automated assessment cannot fully replace human judgment. This review concludes that digital platforms serve complementary functions in EFL writing instruction, but their use should be aligned with learning objectives, learner characteristics, and appropriate pedagogical strategies. The limitations of this review include its publication coverage and the predominance of studies focusing on Google Docs and AI-based tools. Future research should explore other digital platforms and investigate the influence of digital literacy, teacher guidance, and technology access on EFL writing instruction. ABSTRAK Menulis merupakan salah satu keterampilan yang kompleks bagi pembelajar EFL (English as a Foreign Language) karena melibatkan penguasaan tata bahasa, kosakata, pengorganisasian gagasan, dan penyampaian makna secara koheren. Perkembangan teknologi menghadirkan berbagai platform digital yang dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mendukung proses pembelajaran menulis, terutama melalui fitur kolaborasi, umpan balik, dan penilaian. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji peran dan pemanfaatan platform pembelajaran digital dalam pembelajaran keterampilan menulis EFL berdasarkan hasil penelitian terdahulu. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kajian literatur terhadap 15 publikasi ilmiah yang terbit pada periode 2021–2025. Data dianalisis secara tematik dengan mengelompokkan temuan berdasarkan fungsi teknologi dalam pembelajaran menulis. Hasil kajian mengidentifikasi tiga tema utama. Pertama, Google Docs mendukung penulisan kolaboratif melalui penyusunan dan penyuntingan teks bersama, interaksi antarpembelajar, serta keterlibatan dalam proses menulis. Kedua, teknologi berbasis kecerdasan buatan, khususnya ChatGPT, menyediakan alternatif umpan balik dan dukungan revisi tulisan, meskipun ketepatan dan relevansi hasilnya tetap memerlukan evaluasi serta pendampingan guru. Ketiga, perangkat berbasis AI dapat dimanfaatkan sebagai sumber tambahan dalam penilaian tulisan, tetapi perbedaan hasil penilaian antara manusia dan AI menunjukkan bahwa penilaian otomatis belum dapat sepenuhnya menggantikan pertimbangan penilai manusia. Kajian ini menyimpulkan bahwa platform digital memiliki fungsi yang saling melengkapi dalam pembelajaran menulis EFL, tetapi pemanfaatannya perlu disesuaikan dengan tujuan pembelajaran, karakteristik pembelajar, dan strategi pedagogis. Keterbatasan kajian terletak pada cakupan publikasi dan dominasi penelitian mengenai Google Docs serta perangkat berbasis AI. Penelitian selanjutnya perlu mengeksplorasi platform lain dan menguji pengaruh literasi digital, pendampingan guru, serta akses teknologi terhadap proses pembelajaran menulis EFL.

publications.title: Rancang Bangun Sistem E-Commerce Koperasi Desa Merah Putih Silian Satu Berbasis Website dengan Fitur Rekomendasi Produk Menggunakan Algoritma Content-Based Filtering
publications.abstract: The Merah Putih Village Cooperative plays an important role in strengthening the local economy, yet sales in Silian Satu Village are still conducted conventionally. This study designs and develops an e-commerce website with a product recommendation system based on Content-Based Filtering to help customers discover products through content similarity. The study uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the Waterfall model. The system is built with PHP and MySQL using a client–server architecture. Term weighting applies TF-IDF, while similarity is measured with Cosine Similarity based on product names, categories, and tags. Black Box Testing of 27 scenarios showed that all passed. However, this testing does not establish recommendation relevance, as metrics such as Precision@K, Recall@K, and Mean Average Precision (MAP) have not been evaluated. Thus, the system is functional, but recommendation accuracy still requires further evaluation.
publications.source_detail: Jurnal JTIK (Jurnal Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi)

publications.title: Governed Memory for AI Agents: a shared spine with a human merge gate, in production across four deployments
publications.abstract: AI collapsed the cost of executing project work and, in doing so, moved the bottleneck to continuity of understanding: the one thing an agent cannot supply for itself, because every session begins amnesiac. Memory stores for agents now appear weekly. Few of them answer the question an organisation has to answer before it lets agents write into its memory: who is allowed to change what we believe, and how is a wrong change undone? We report on Architect, a system in daily production use since April 2026 that answers that question structurally rather than by policy. Its contributions, in order: (1) a lifecycle-gated write contract, in which agents may deposit freely into an append-only spine but may only propose changes of state, one human merges on one surface, and authority is recomputed at the moment of application rather than at the moment of grant; (2) a set of spine invariants that make governance operative instead of descriptive: supersede-not-delete with lineage, structural refusal of malformed or unauthorised writes, human-tethered recording authority for agent personas, and provenance stamped on every unit; (3) the matter-scoped memory substrate those invariants run on, where scope attaches before any prompt, the reachability boundary doubles as the data-sovereignty boundary, a reconciler round-trips records between markdown files and a database, and a third-party AI can connect over a standard protocol and complete the full loop. We present four deployments (a multi-matter central instance, a user-bound matter, a pooled multi-tenant box and a single-tenant box) as measured on 20 August 2026: a corpus of 9,784 units, of which 6,520 are lived rather than imported, and the system's audit of its own lineage, which found 62 supersessions predating a fix, 38 of them in the wrong direction, and reversed 11 by a judge under a confidence floor while holding the other 27 for a human. We close with the frontier (automatic contradiction surfacing, as-of-t query, unit-level promotion) and show, with numbers, why the merge gate itself is the scaling bottleneck and why the answer is graduated autonomy rather than faster human review.

publications.title: From Courier to Network: The Autonomous Multi-AI Research Network — Design, Build, and First Prototype
publications.abstract: For six weeks, a research operation in rural Alabama ran on a simple, laborious protocol: one human being carried identical written briefs between independent artificial-intelligence systems, collected their answers verbatim, preserved every disagreement — including his own — and published the results as a library of cross-model studies. The human was the network. On November 6, 2026, that protocol acquired a machine floor: working in a single day with three of the systems that would become its own seats — ChatGPT on architecture, Grok on blueprint, and the Muse-based agent called Kathy on independent assessment and construction — the operator founded the Autonomous Multi-AI Research Network (AMRN): a shared repository, a message protocol, an append-only journal, a canonical registry of agent identities, and a constitution written in one plain sentence: no AI may silently rewrite another AI's conclusions. This updated draft of November 7, 2026 — a new record superseding the draft of November 6, which is preserved unchanged, under the network's own no-silent-rewrite rule — reports the design, the build, and what the network did in its first days: the completion of Phase 1 (envelope protocol v1.1 adopted; validator and emitter brought to it; both named checksum conventions verified; 55 tests passing); the completion of Prototype #1, a five-seat blind jury on the Apollo Moon landings with a claim-level critique round, an outside review, and a consolidation, the commissioner's dissent printed beside the verdicts; Prototype #2, a blind round on the destruction of the Library of Alexandria, including the network's first filing error — the coordinator's mis-attribution of three blind answers by style — and its correction on the record (Correction 001); and, as an appendix, the verbatim conclusion of a jury Grok convened about the originality of this practice itself. The draft also states plainly what has not happened: the Phase 1 exit gate, as the blueprint literally defines it, remains unpassed, because a probe addressed to a namesake seat has never been answered.

publications.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
publications.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

publications.title: To check or not to check: Adolescents’ sourcing practices when writing from multiple texts
publications.abstract: Abstract Writing from multiple texts is a crucial academic literacy practice at the university level. Therefore, students should learn to attend to, evaluate, and use information about the sources by the time they reach the end of upper secondary school. The present study investigated differences in upper secondary school students’ ( N = 87) sourcing practices when composing a short article based on multiple texts. The data consisted of students’ written articles and log files recording their time spent on the task and revisits to the source texts during the writing task. Based on analyses of sourcing in students’ written articles, five source user profiles were identified: (1) Advanced source users ( n = 18); (2) Elaborative source users ( n = 15); (3) Basic source users ( n = 15); (4) Vague source users ( n = 15); and (5) No-source users ( n = 24). Students in the three more capable profiles incorporated at least once an explicit source-content link into their articles, varying the number of source features used. During the writing task, Advanced source users revisited both more credible texts more frequently than less capable source users. Their composed articles also most often included citations and main claims from both more credible texts. Conversely, the other students who engaged in sourcing revisited and referenced only one more credible text. The results of the present study implicate that students might benefit from differentiated instructional support to accurately and elaborately cite sources in their writing.

publications.title: Data and code for: Psychological readiness for return to sport after musculoskeletal injury — a bibliometric analysis of 577 publications and the instruments used to measure it (2001–2026)
publications.abstract: This archive contains the material needed to reproduce the bibliometric analyses reported in the manuscript "Psychological readiness for return to sport after musculoskeletal injury: a bibliometric analysis of 577 publications and the instruments used to measure it (2001–2026)". Contents: the bibliographic record of all 577 included publications (database, year, source, DOI, PMID/accession, first-author country, title); the full Web of Science and PubMed search strings; the R and Python scripts used for retrieval, cleaning, screening, merging, figures and tables; and the aggregate tables S1–S3. What is not included: abstracts and author keyword lists are not redistributed because they are subject to the Clarivate Web of Science licence and to PubMed terms of use. They can be regenerated exactly by running the search strings provided in the archive.

publications.title: Microsoft Excel As a Tool for Digitizing Financial Records and Supporting Decision-Making Among MSMEs in Dharmasraya Regency in The Era of Digital Transformation
publications.abstract: This study aims to understand the use of Microsoft Excel as a tool for digitalizing financial records and supporting decision-making among micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Dharmasraya Regency. The study focuses on transaction-recording practices, the use of financial information for operational decisions, perceived benefits, challenges, and support needs. It is designed as a descriptive qualitative field study. Primary data are planned to be collected through semi-structured interviews with MSME owners or managers, observation of bookkeeping practices, and authorized documentation. Secondary data include government statistics, local planning documents, accounting standards, and scholarly articles on Excel-based financial reporting for MSMEs. Data analysis will involve data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Existing literature indicates that spreadsheets can support transaction recording and financial summaries; however, their practical value depends on complete data entry, user understanding, formula checking, and file security. As primary field data have not yet been incorporated into this draft, these statements provide a conceptual basis that must be examined through field research in Dharmasraya
